subject: Right factor coding for phenotypic trajectory

messages.author: 9514786479a8771a
messages.subject: Right factor coding for phenotypic trajectory
parts:
Dear all, 
I'm conducting a Phenotypic Trajectory Analysis to test how a multivariate phenotype changes between two groups (rural vs urban populations of a frog species) throughout ontogeny (three age groups, inferred from Lines of Arrested Growth). 

My question is: Do I need to code the ontogeny as an ordered factor before plughing it into the model in lm.rrpp? The age variable is coded as 1-2y, 3-4y, and 5-6y. I'm running the analysis in two steps, as in the function example:

mod_biom <- lm.rrpp(scores_biom~Local*Age, data = biom)
summary(mod_biom)

TA_biom <- trajectory.analysis(mod_biom, groups = biom$Local, traj.pts = biom$Age)

Thank you in advance,
Diogo

Diogo

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Right factor coding for phenotypic trajectory
parts:
Diogo,

 

Yes. For the design you described, you should make this an ordered factor.

 

For the plots, try ‘cex=0’ to remove the dots.

 

Dean

Diogo,

Check the example for trajectory.analysis and where the plot is originally made — TP <- plot(TA, …) — use cex = 0 as Dean suggested or type = ‘n’ and no points will be made. Since add.trajectories has its own arguments, trajectories can be added to an empty plot. 

Mike

Thanks a lot Dean and Mike for the quick reply! The plotting worked like a charm with this tweak, but somehow I couldn't get the age classes to work properly as an ordered factor. I believe my data are a simpler case of the snake head shape example of Collyer & Adams 2013, because I only have two populations (rural vs urban) with three age classes. Do you perhaps mind sharing the code you used to run this example and make Fig. 5?

- I did this:

germ_cells_p$Age <- factor(germ_cells_p$Age, levels = c("1-2y", "3-4y", "5-6y"), ordered = TRUE)

> str(germ_cells_p$Age)
 Ord.factor w/ 3 levels "1-2y"<"3-4y"<..: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 ...

> class(germ_cells_p$Age)
[1] "ordered" "factor" 

- This is a glimpse of my data

    Local Age   gonia  cyte  tyde sperm
   <fct> <ord> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
 1 BEP   3-4y   3.19 14.9   2.13  79.8
 2 BEP   3-4y   7.32 13.7   2.44  76.6
 3 BEP   3-4y   3.07  3.95  0.44  92.5
 4 BEP   3-4y   9.04 16.5   3.72  70.7

- This is a multivariate dataset describing the density of each germ cell type, so I run a PCA for compositional data

only_Germcells <- as.data.frame(germ_cells_p[,c(3:6)])
pca_GermCells <- princomp(acomp(only_Germcells))
scores_germCells <- pca_GermCells$scores

Then built the linear model and plugged it into the trajectory analysis itself:

mod_germs <- lm.rrpp(germ_scores~Local*Age, data = dd)

TA_germ <- trajectory.analysis(mod_germs, groups = dd$Local, traj.pts = dd$Age)

plot_ta_germ <- plot(TA_germ,  type = "n", col = "gray", xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1,1))

add.trajectories(plot_ta_germ, traj.pch = c(21, 22),traj.col = c("blue", "black"), start.bg = "black", end.bg = "red",traj.lty = c(2,1))

But somehow the sequence of age classes does not appear correctly in the trajectory plot...

Any ideas?
